In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=1-2{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{4x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(1-2{x}^{2})(\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})-\int (\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})(-4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}}{4}+\int x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{4x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})-\int (\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{4x}}{4}-\frac{1}{4}\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{4x}}{4}-\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}+C \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(4x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{(1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}}{4}+(\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(4x-1)+C) \\  & =\frac{(1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}}{4}+\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(4x-1)+C \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(-8{x}^{2}+4x+3)+C.\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}\int ({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =({t}^{2}+1)(\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\int t\,{e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\displaystyle\int t\,e^{2t+1}\,\textrm{d}t.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}={e}^{2t+1}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t=\int {e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t=\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int t\,{e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =(t)(\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})(1)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is a constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\int t\,{e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-(\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}+D) \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}+\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}-D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}(2{t}^{2}-2t+3)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C = -{D}.$ 

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & ={[\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}(2{t}^{2}-2t+3)]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{{e}^{2(1)+1}}{4}(2(1)^{2}-2(1)+3))-(\frac{{e}^{2(0)+1}}{4}(2(0)^{2}-2(0)+3)) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3}}{4}(2-2+3)-\frac{e}{4}(0-0+3) \\  & =\frac{3{e}^{3}}{4}-\frac{3e}{4} \\  & =\frac{3{e}^{3}-3e}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we define

$$

$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2})(\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))-\int (\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{3}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\displaystyle \int x\sin(3x) \textrm{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x=-\,\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =x(-\,\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))-\int (-\,\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))\cdot 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{3}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x \\  & =-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{3}(\frac{1}{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))+{C}_{1} \\  & =-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{9}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+{C}_{1}\,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C_1$ is a constant of integration.
So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{3}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{3}(-\,\frac{1}{3}\,x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{1}{9}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+{C}_{1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{2}{9}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-\frac{2}{27}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\frac{2{C}_{1}}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{27}((9{x}^{2}-2)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))+C,\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of a Logarithmic Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2} & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=32{x}^{3} & \,⟹\,v=\int 32{x}^{3}\text{d}x=8{x}^{4}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 32{x}^{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & ={(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}(8{x}^{4})-\int (8{x}^{4})(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x})\text{d}x \\  & =8{x}^{4}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-16\int {x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\displaystyle\int {x^3\ln(x)} \textrm{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x) & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={x}^{3} & \,⟹\,v=\int {x}^{3}\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)(\frac{{x}^{4}}{4})-\int (\frac{{x}^{4}}{4})(\frac{1}{x})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{4}-\frac{1}{4}\int {x}^{3}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{4}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{16}+{C}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

where $C_1$ is an integral constant. So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 32{x}^{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\text{d}x & =8{x}^{4}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-16\int {x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}x \\  & =8{x}^{4}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-16(\frac{{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{4}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{16}+{C}_{1}) \\  & =8{x}^{4}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-4{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+{x}^{4}-16{C}_{1} \\  & ={x}^{4}(8{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)+C\,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C = -4C_1.$ Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}32{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}x & ={{x}^{4}(8{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =[(e)^{4}(8{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(e))}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)+1)]-[(1)^{4}(8{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(1))}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+1)] \\  & =[{e}^{4}(8-4+1)]-1 \\  & =5{e}^{4}-1.\end{aligned}
$$
